battle.name: 羅德島圍城戰
battle.brief: 公元前305年夏，安提柯一世率希臘化聯軍大舉圍攻羅德島城，試圖斬斷托勒密一世的東地中海支點；圍城歷時約一年，德米特里奧斯的巨型攻城塔幾乎破牆，終為羅德島人以火攻焚毀。卡面的埃及月牙劍在公元前305年早已退為古物，但它源出的埃及，正是本戰役中被遠道聯軍逼到海角的一方。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 羅德島圍城戰（公元前305年至前304年）是繼業者戰爭後期，安提柯王朝與托勒密王朝爭奪東地中海的關鍵一役，交戰主體是安提柯的希臘化聯軍與羅德島城邦。安提柯一方集結的是以馬其頓重裝步兵為骨幹的多國聯軍：安提柯一世自率主力，其弟腓力另率分艦隊，腓尼基人、塞浦路斯人與其他希臘城邦提供水手與小型船隻，另有象兵、輕裝兵與攻城工匠隨軍；全軍配備大量攻城機械，由專門的工匠隊操作。羅德島一方是城邦公民軍與外來雇傭兵組成的守備部隊，另有城內船塢建造的戰艦與技術人員——熟悉配重式投射器、投石機與防禦機械的工程師——共同守城。開戰前羅德島還向埃及求援，托勒密一世派出艦隊與援軍前往解圍，但該支分隊在科斯島與克尼多斯島一線被截住，未能進入羅德港。戰局本質上是一場封鎖與消耗：安提柯靠制海權切斷島城的糧食與木材，靠圍城牆把守軍釘在城內；羅德島則靠城牆高度、海上襲擾與反擊爭取時間。這場戰爭同時是三種軍事的交錯——海軍封鎖、攻城機械對抗城防、以及兩位繼業者君主對小亞細亞與東地中海主導權的賭注。
countriesEn: The Siege of Rhodes (305–304 BC) was a decisive engagement of the later Wars of the Diadochi, in which the Antigonid house and the Ptolemaic house fought over the eastern Mediterranean; the belligerents proper were Antigonus's Hellenic league army and the city-state of Rhodes. On Antigonus's side stood a multi-national coalition built around the Macedonian phalanx: Antigonus I commanded the main body in person, his brother Philip brought a separate squadron of the fleet, and Phoenicians, Cypriots and other Greek cities supplied crews and smaller vessels, with elephants, light infantry and the siege-engine crews travelling with the army; the whole force was equipped with an abundance of siege machines operated by dedicated teams of artisans. On the Rhodian side the garrison was composed of the city's citizen troops together with hired mercenaries, backed by warships built in the city's own dockyards and by technicians who knew the heavy counterweight engines, stone-throwers and defensive machines of the age, including engineers skilled in traction artillery and in swivel-mounted bolt throwers. Before the war began Rhodes had appealed to Egypt for help, and Ptolemy I sent a squadron and a relief force across the sea, but that detachment was intercepted in the neighbourhood of Cos and Cnidus and never entered the harbour of Rhodes. In its essentials the siege was a contest of blockade and attrition: Antigonus relied on command of the sea to cut the island's grain and timber, and on the circumvallation to pin the garrison inside the walls, while Rhodes relied on the height of its walls, on harassment at sea and on sorties to buy time. Three kinds of war were braided together here — a naval blockade, a duel between siege machinery and city defences, and a wager between two Diadochi monarchs over the mastery of Asia Minor and the eastern Mediterranean.
people: 安提柯一世·獨眼（Antigonus I Monophthalmus）是本戰役的統帥，這位老牌馬其頓將領以全軍統帥的身份指揮大局，攻城所用的機械、封鎖線的佈置與最後的外交收買都出自他的決策。執行者是其子德米特里奧斯·波利奧刻忒斯（Demetrius Poliorcetes），希臘世界稱他為「攻城者」：他主持設計並組裝那座高約三十六公尺、鐵板包覆的 Helepolis 攻城塔，以及撞擊城牆的 Epibole 與撞門的 sarapax；傳統記載把這套機械的構圖與施工歸於亞歷山大里亞的工程師歐達摩斯，狄奧多羅斯與維特魯威留下了尺寸與構造的細節。城內的主導者是羅德島的將領與工匠團隊，其中負責火攻的是被記錄下來的一支小組——他們在牆上選定城塔（Dioceles）這一段最脆弱的位置，把以風箱與壓縮空氣推動的管狀吹火裝置架在牆頭，火焰沿地面直噴攻城塔底部。留下最完整記述的是希臘史家波利比烏斯，他在《歷史》第二卷逐日描寫圍城始末，包括攻城塔被焚、海軍夜襲與和談條件；狄奧多羅斯·西庫路斯在《圖書館史》二十卷提供另一套細節；維特魯威在《建築十卷》第十卷則從工匠角度分析這兩種機械的優劣，並指出羅德島人的反制裝置如何用風力與壓縮空氣把火焰吹向攻城塔底部。
peopleEn: Antigonus I Monophthalmus, the One-Eyed, was the supreme commander of the siege: this veteran Macedonian general directed the entire army in the field, and the choice of machinery, the disposition of the blockade and the final diplomatic purchase of a settlement all came out of his own decisions. The execution was entrusted to his son Demetrius Poliorcetes, whom the Greek world nicknamed the Besieger: he presided over the design and assembly of the Helepolis, the siege tower standing about thirty-six metres high and clad in iron plate, together with the wall-striker Epibole and the battering ram sarapax; tradition credits the layout and construction of the machines to Eudamus of Alexandria, and Diodorus Siculus and Vitruvius preserve the dimensions and the structural details. On the Rhodian side the guiding figures were the city's commanders and its corps of engineers, and among them the men credited with the fire attack — a small team that selected the weakest stretch of the wall, the sector of the Dioceles tower, and mounted on it a tube fed by bellows and compressed air that played flame against the advancing engine. The fullest record comes from the Greek historian Polybius, whose second book describes the siege day by day, including the burning of the tower, the night attack on the fleet and the terms of the settlement; Diodorus Siculus supplies a rival set of details in the twentieth book of his Library; Vitruvius, in the tenth book of De Architectura, analyses both machines from the craftsman's point of view and shows how the Rhodian counter-device used wind and compressed air to drive the fire into the base of the engine.
kits: 卡面兵器是埃及月牙劍（Khopesh）：約公元前1500年已在埃及出現，外彎的單刃短劍，砍入之後不必把刃拔出，因此適合在近身混戰中連續劈擊。公元前305年，這種形制的劍早已不是埃及軍的制式裝備——埃及步兵此時裝備的是直身雙刃的鴨嘴劍與科皮斯式彎刀，月牙劍退居宗教儀式、象形文字與文物之中，本戰役的兩軍都沒有使用月牙劍作戰。把它放進這場戰爭的體系裡看，是要看它源出的那支軍隊：埃及的托勒密一世正是羅德島一方的實際庇護者，而本戰役的開端正是一支從小亞細亞方向捲來的聯軍。真正決定攻防的是攻城機械：安提柯一方有 Helepolis 攻城塔、Epibole 城牆撞擊機、sarapax 撞門槌、車輪式龜甲塔與各型投石機、弩砲；羅德島一方有城牆頭的配重式投射器、弓與弩、從塔頂傾倒的滾石與沸水，以及對付攻城塔的燃料與黏土防護物。海戰方面，兩方都備有大型划槳戰艦，羅德島船隊自備撞角與投石，港內還備有火船用的油脂。海運亦決定補給：安提柯的艦隊必須從小亞細亞運來木材、繩索、攻城機零件與糧食，羅德島的木材儲備與糧食存量則直接決定能撐多久。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a sickle-shaped single-edged short sword that had already appeared in Egypt around 1500 BC: because the blade is curved, a blow that lands does not have to be wrenched free, which suits repeated hacking at close quarters. By 305 BC the form was no longer standard equipment of any Egyptian army — Egyptian infantry of that day carried straight double-edged blades of the duckbill type and the curved kopis, while the khopesh had retreated into ritual, hieroglyphic tradition and the museum case; neither side in this siege fought with khopesh. To place it in the order of battle of this war means looking at the people it came from: the Egypt of Ptolemy I was the actual protector of Rhodes, while the army that came over the sea to crush the island was a coalition drawn from the rivals of Egypt and of Asia Minor. What actually decided the attack and the defence was the siege machinery. Antigonus had the Helepolis tower, the Epibole wall-striker, the sarapax ram, wheeled testudo sheds and a full range of stone-throwers and bolt-shooters; Rhodes had the counterweight traction engines on the ramparts, bows and crossbows, rolling stones and boiling liquids poured from the towers, together with fuel and clay screens to shield the wall. At sea both sides fielded large oared warships; the Rhodian squadron carried rams and stone-throwers of its own, and the harbour was stocked with the oil needed for fire-ships. Sea transport governed the logistics as well: Antigonus's fleet had to bring timber, rope, the parts of the siege engines and grain across from Asia Minor, and the island's stocks of timber and provisions decided exactly how long the city could hold out.
tactics: 安提柯的圍城分三層：先以艦隊封鎖羅德港，切斷島城與外界的聯絡；再築環形包圍牆，把羅德島城連同其郊區圈在內，只留一個受控的入口；最後才把攻城機械推到牆下。進攻以攻城塔為主軸，每次只推一段距離，待塔身停穩、位置校準後才讓塔上的投射器與撞槌開火，試圖在城牆上開出缺口；安提柯在缺口處即以土袋與木柵搶修，防止守軍反攻。守方的對應是分工：城牆各段配備投石機與弓箭手壓制塔頂與塔側的進攻人員，專人修補被撞出的缺口並在缺口頂上加築遮蔽；海上有巡邏小艇監視封鎖線，伺機襲擊停泊的運輸船與在港內錨泊的戰艦。關鍵的轉折在於一次火攻：羅德島人選中最薄弱的城塔段，把以風箱與壓縮空氣推動的管狀吹火裝置架在牆上，火焰沿地面直噴攻城塔底部的柴堆與帆布索具，把這座三十六公尺高的木鐵結構燒成骨架；同時守軍出城反擊，燒掉安提柯營中大量帳篷與器材。此後安提柯改為長期圍困，不再急於強攻。
tacticsEn: Antigonus's siege worked in three layers. First the fleet sealed the harbour of Rhodes and cut the island off from the world; next a ring of circumvallation was thrown up, enclosing the city and its surroundings and leaving only a single controlled entrance; only then were the engines brought up to the wall. The attack turned on the tower, which was advanced a stage at a time, halted while the crews checked its position, and only then permitted to open fire with its own artillery and ram in the hope of opening a breach; where a breach did appear Antigonus's men rushed to plug it with sandbags and timber so that the defenders could not sally out through it. The defence was organised by task: each stretch of wall carried stone-throwers and archers to pin the crews and the artillery on the flanks of the engine, dedicated parties repaired the masonry that had been knocked out, and covered working parties built overhead protection above the new damage. Small boats patrolled outside the blockade line, watching for an opportunity to strike at the supply ships and at the warships lying at anchor in the harbour. The turning point came with a fire attack. The Rhodians chose the weakest sector of the wall, mounted a tube that blew flame by bellows and compressed air, and drove the fire straight along the ground into the stacked timber and the canvas lashings under the base of the tower, burning this thirty-six-metre frame of wood and iron down to its skeleton; at the same moment the garrison sallied out and fired the camp of Antigonus, destroying a great quantity of tents and equipment. After that Antigonus settled down to a blockade and no longer pressed for an immediate breach.
data: 兵力與船數以波利比烏斯的記述為準：安提柯自率本部約三萬六千名步兵與四千名騎兵，連同其弟腓力所率的分艦隊，全部海軍合計約二百五十艘戰艦，其中安提柯本人指揮約一百五十艘；羅德島守軍的總數史籍未留下可靠記載，只能確認由公民兵、雇傭兵與工匠組成。圍城自公元前305年夏開打，至前304年春解除，歷時約一年。機械尺寸以狄奧多羅斯為主：Helepolis 高約三十六公尺、寬約二十公尺，底部包鐵，需要約三千人分組推動，並以多組絞盤控制進退；撞門槌 sarapax 長約九公尺，可反覆撞擊同一處磚石。日期方面，波利比烏斯把火攻與反擊記在前304年夏，通行換算的日期為公元前304年5月24日。損失方面，羅德島人夜襲安提柯在港內錨泊的船隊，據記載燒毀或擊毀三十六艘戰艦；攻城塔焚毀後，安提柯營中損失的人數與器械沒有留下確數。和談的價碼也有記載：羅德島方面須支付約一千塔蘭特白銀作為贖金，安提柯則保證撤軍並不干預島城的內政。
dataEn: For numbers of men and ships one must follow Polybius: Antigonus brought a main body of about thirty-six thousand foot and four thousand horse, and with the squadron of his brother Philip the whole fleet numbered about two hundred and fifty warships, of which Antigonus himself commanded some hundred and fifty; no reliable figure survives for the Rhodian garrison, which consisted of citizens, mercenaries and artisans. The siege opened in the summer of 305 BC and was lifted in the spring of 304 BC, lasting roughly a year. For the dimensions of the machines Diodorus is the principal authority: the Helepolis stood about thirty-six metres high and twenty metres wide, its base sheathed in iron, it needed some three thousand men grouped in teams to move it, and it was controlled by several sets of capstans; the battering ram sarapax was about nine metres long and could be worked again and again on the same stretch of masonry. As for dates, Polybius places the fire attack and the sortie in the summer of 304 BC, and the day usually given for it is 24 May 304 BC. On losses, the Rhodians fell upon the fleet at anchor in the harbour by night and are recorded as having burnt or sunk thirty-six warships; when the tower went up in flame no exact count of the men and equipment lost in Antigonus's camp was kept. The price of the settlement is also recorded: Rhodes was to pay roughly a thousand talents of silver as a ransom, on the figure given by Polybius, while Antigonus gave his word to withdraw and to leave the island's internal affairs alone.
cause: 羅德島城邦的地理位置決定了它捲入爭霸：它扼住小亞細亞西南端的航路，靠近通往埃及的近海航道，安提柯若要保有小亞細亞，就必須讓這座島城留在自己手裡。公元前305年，安提柯任命的總督米特里達特斯在島上推行強硬政策，羅德島人起義將他逐出城，隨後轉而向埃及的托勒密一世求援，兩城邦結為同盟，羅德島的戰艦編入托勒密的地中海體系。此時希臘世界已進入繼業者戰爭的收尾階段：安提柯的亞洲王國與托勒密、塞琉古在巴勒斯坦與小亞細亞互相進逼，而塞琉古被迫放棄巴比倫、退回中亞，安提柯得以抽出手來。羅德島的叛離等於在安提柯的側翼插上一把刀，於是安提柯在公元前305年夏集中遠征兵力——本部兵員、海軍、攻城機械與隨軍工匠一次到齊，遠道越過小亞細亞——把羅德島城團團圍住。他打的算盤很清楚：只要拿下列島城，愛琴海東南與東地中海的航線就重新回到他手裡；托勒密在埃及的基地也就直接暴露在攻擊之下。
causeEn: The geographical position of Rhodes settled its place in the struggle: it commands the sea lanes off the south-western tip of Asia Minor, close to the coastal route to Egypt, and Antigonus could not keep Asia Minor unless the island city stayed in his hands. In 305 BC the governor Mithridates whom Antigonus had appointed ruled the island harshly, the Rhodians rose and drove him out of the city, and they then turned to Ptolemy I of Egypt for help, the two city-states forming an alliance and the Rhodian squadrons being folded into the Ptolemaic maritime system. By this time the Greek world had reached the closing stage of the Wars of the Diadochi: Antigonus's kingdom of Asia and Ptolemy and Seleucus were closing on one another in Palestine and Asia Minor, and since Seleucus had been forced to abandon Babylon and withdraw to Central Asia, Antigonus was able to free his hands. The defection of Rhodes was a knife at Antigonus's flank, so in the summer of 305 BC he concentrated his expeditionary force — infantry, horse, fleet, siege engines and the artisans who served them — crossed Asia Minor and closed around the city of Rhodes. His reckoning was plain: once the island city fell, the sea lanes of the south-eastern Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean would return to his hands, and the Egyptian base of Ptolemy would stand directly exposed to attack.
impact: 這場圍城沒有分出勝負，卻改變了東地中海的權力版圖。羅德島守住了，使得安提柯沒能打開通往埃及的跳板，托勒密得以鞏固其在塞浦路斯與黎凡特海岸的據點，把埃及與地中海東岸的航線連成一體；對安提柯而言，攻城的失敗也讓他無法在亞洲方向騰出手來，兩年後塞琉古東返、奪回巴比倫時，他仍陷在希臘與小亞細亞的糾葛裡。技術史上，這一役是希臘大型攻城機的頂點與分水嶺：德米特里奧斯的 Helepolis 雖在羅德島折戟，同一套機械在同年的薩拉米斯圍城戰中卻成功破城，說明希臘化君主之間的攻城技術競爭已進入以專門設計的巨型機械為核心的階段；狄奧多羅斯與維特魯威的記述也讓這兩座機械成為後世兵書與工程學常被引用的範例。羅德島在解圍之後獲得實質獨立，趁著兩強相持擴大自己的商船隊與航線，逐步成為東地中海重要的商業與藝術中心；城邦在城內興建公共建築、培育雕塑與鑄幣，日後傲立島上的羅德島巨像正是這段繁榮的產物，而圍城的記憶則被寫進了城邦的錢幣與守城女神像之中。
impactEn: The siege ended without a decision, and yet it reshaped the balance of power in the eastern Mediterranean. Rhodes held, so Antigonus never opened the door into Egypt; Ptolemy was able to consolidate his positions in Cyprus and on the Levantine coast, and to link Egypt with the sea routes of the eastern Mediterranean in a single system. For Antigonus the failure to take the city also meant that he could not free his hands in Asia, and two years later, when Seleucus returned east and recovered Babylon, he was still tangled in the affairs of Greece and Asia Minor. In the history of technique this campaign was both the summit and the turning point of Hellenic siegecraft: Demetrius's Helepolis was wrecked at Rhodes, yet the same machines broke a city at the siege of Salamis in the same year, showing that the competition between the Diadochi kings had already entered the stage in which purpose-built giant engines were the centre of the business. The accounts of Diodorus and Vitruvius made these two machines standard examples quoted by later writers on fortification and engineering. Freed from the siege, Rhodes obtained de facto independence, enlarged her merchant fleet and her trading routes, and became an important commercial and artistic centre of the eastern Mediterranean; the city built public works, fostered sculpture and coinage, and the great colossus that was later to stand on the island was the product of that prosperity, while the memory of the siege was carried in the city's coinage and in the figure of its guardian goddess.
result: 到公元前304年春，羅德島城仍在牆上，攻城塔被燒成骨架、港內三十六艘戰艦被毀，安提柯的攻城計畫徹底失敗。波利比烏斯記載，羅德島人在走投無路時主動求和，同意支付約一千塔蘭特白銀作為贖金，安提柯則撤軍並承認島城的獨立；後續局勢變化——塞琉古在亞洲得手的消息傳來、托勒密自海陸兩面向小亞細亞施壓——讓安提柯更急於回師，圍城因此以交易收場而非以破城收場。守方代價高昂：城市的補給在一年圍困中被消耗殆盡，郊區果園與部分房屋被安提柯的軍隊徵用或毀壞，圍城之後羅德島城的防衛仍要長期維持。但從結果看，這是希臘化世界少數幾場「城市守住、圍城者敗退」的戰役之一；德米特里奧斯本人隨後把經驗帶往薩拉米斯，在那裡以攻城塔與撞槌取得破城之功，也把希臘化君主「以機械攻城」的風氣推到頂點。
resultEn: In the spring of 304 BC the walls of Rhodes were still standing: the siege tower had been burnt to its skeleton, thirty-six warships had been lost in the harbour, and Antigonus's plan of assault had failed outright. Polybius records that the Rhodians, seeing no way out, sued for peace and agreed to pay a ransom of roughly a thousand talents of silver, while Antigonus withdrew and recognised the independence of the city; the turn in the wider situation — the news of Seleucus's success in Asia and the pressure Ptolemy exerted towards Asia Minor by land and sea — made Antigonus more eager to march home, so the siege ended in a transaction rather than in a breach. The victor's bill was heavy: the city's supplies were consumed to the last during the year of blockade, the orchards and some of the houses outside the walls were requisitioned or destroyed by Antigonus's troops, and the defences of Rhodes had to be maintained at great expense for long afterwards. In outcome, however, this is one of the few sieges in the Hellenistic world that the besieged won and the besieger broke off. Demetrius carried the lessons of the campaign on to Salamis, where he used tower and ram to breach a city, and pushed the fashion of the Hellenistic king who assaults by machinery to its extreme.
